title: Does ChatGPT Give the Same Answer to Everyone? No, Here's Why
excerpt: No. ChatGPT answers vary with randomness, model version, memory, context, search and location. Try a simple test and learn how to measure AI visibility.
keywords: does ChatGPT give the same answer to everyone
does ChatGPT give the same answers to everyone
does ChatGPT give the same answers
why does ChatGPT give different answers to the same question
why do LLMs give different responses to the same prompt
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
No, ChatGPT does not give the same answer to everyone. Even [OpenAI's own documentation](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) notes that, because there are many plausible ways to complete a sentence, "the same question may yield different answers across different queries." On top of that built-in randomness, answers shift with the model version, your memory and custom instructions, earlier messages in the chat, whether a web search ran, your location and features that roll out to some accounts before others.

For everyday use that variety is mostly harmless. For brands it changes how visibility should be measured: one screenshot of ChatGPT recommending (or ignoring) you proves very little. This article explains each cause of variation, gives you a simple experiment to see it yourself and shows how to measure visibility in a way that holds up.

## Why ChatGPT's answers differ: the eight main causes

### 1. Sampling and temperature (built-in randomness)

ChatGPT writes a response one token (a word or part of a word) at a time. At each step the model has a range of likely next tokens, and it *samples* from them instead of always picking the single most likely one. [OpenAI's help center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) describes this "inherent element of randomness" directly.

Developers using OpenAI's API can see the dial that controls this. The `temperature` setting ranges from 0 to 2: according to [OpenAI's API reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create), higher values such as 0.8 make output more random, while lower values such as 0.2 make it more focused and deterministic. As far as we can see, the consumer ChatGPT app has no temperature setting for users, so some run-to-run variation is simply part of the product.

Small early differences compound. If one run happens to name Brand A first, the rest of the answer tends to build on that choice, so two runs can diverge noticeably even from an identical prompt.

### 2. Model versions

Different ChatGPT models produce different answers, and the models themselves change over time. OpenAI's [text generation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text) advises pinning production apps to specific model snapshots because "even different snapshots of models within the same family could produce different results." In our experience, the default model in ChatGPT changes when OpenAI ships new ones, and new models can reach different accounts at different times. When a recommendation list suddenly reshuffles, a model change is a common suspect; our guide to [AI model drift detection](/blog/ai-model-drift-detection) covers how to spot it.

### 3. Memory and personalization

When [memory](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt) is on, ChatGPT can use relevant information from past chats, saved memories, files in your Library and connected apps (such as Gmail) to personalize responses, depending on plan and region. If you've told ChatGPT you run a vegan bakery in Chicago, it can factor that in. If you've spent months asking about your own company, it may bring your brand up more readily for you than for a stranger.

### 4. Custom instructions

Custom instructions are text you write once that ChatGPT considers in every response. [OpenAI's custom instructions article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8096356-custom-instructions-for-chatgpt) says changes to them are applied immediately across all chats. An instruction like "I'm a B2B buyer in Germany, keep answers short" will change which products get suggested and how they are described.

### 5. Conversation context

Everything earlier in the same chat steers what comes next. Ask about "affordable tools" three messages ago and later recommendations will lean cheap. Mention a competitor and it becomes part of the context. That is why tests should always start in a fresh chat.

### 6. Search on or off, and a changing web

Answers based only on training data reflect what the model learned up to its cutoff. When ChatGPT searches the web, it rewrites your question into search queries, reads current pages and cites them. According to OpenAI's [web search help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), ChatGPT may search automatically when a question would benefit from current information, and users can also start a search manually. Whether a search runs, which queries it sends and which pages rank that day all affect the answer, and web results themselves change constantly. (For how retrieval picks which products to mention, see [how AI search engines recommend products](/blog/how-ai-search-engines-recommend-products).) For the full picture of these inputs, see [where does ChatGPT get its information?](/blog/where-does-chatgpt-get-its-information)

### 7. Location and language

[OpenAI's web search help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt) says ChatGPT collects approximate location from your IP address and may include it in search queries; device location sharing is optional and off by default. Asking in Spanish, or from London rather than Dallas, can surface different sources and different brands, especially for local or regional products.

### 8. Gradual rollouts and account differences

[OpenAI's memory article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt) notes that memory features and controls "can vary by plan, region, platform, and workspace settings" and that some may not be available for an account yet. Features, tools and models reach different users at different times, so two people can be using a slightly different ChatGPT without knowing it.

## Which causes you can control

| Cause | Changes answers for... | Can you control it when testing? |
|---|---|---|
| Sampling randomness | Every run, even for the same person | No (in the app). Run prompts repeatedly instead |
| Model version | Users on different models; everyone after updates | Partly. Note which model answered |
| Memory | Logged-in users with memory on | Yes. Log out or use an unpersonalized Temporary Chat |
| Custom instructions | Users who set them | Yes. Same as above, or clear them |
| Conversation context | Every message after the first | Yes. Use a fresh chat for every prompt |
| Search on/off and web results | Prompts that trigger search | Partly. Record whether citations appeared |
| Location and language | Search-enabled and local queries | Partly. Keep language fixed; note your location or VPN |
| Rollouts and plan differences | Different accounts | Partly. Test with consistent accounts |

## Try it yourself: a 20-minute experiment

You don't need to take anyone's word for this. Pick one category question your buyers would ask, for example:

```
What are the best project management tools for a 10-person marketing agency?
```

Then run it under four conditions:

1. **Logged out.** Open ChatGPT in a private browser window without signing in. Ask the question in a new chat. Repeat 5 times, opening a fresh chat each time.
2. **Unpersonalized Temporary Chat.** Signed in, start a Temporary Chat and choose **Unpersonalized** before your first message. This matters: OpenAI's [Temporary Chat documentation](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8914046-temporary-chat-in-chatgpt) says a Temporary Chat can be *personalized* (using your memories and custom instructions) unless you choose Unpersonalized, and you can't change it after the chat starts. Repeat 5 times.
3. **Your normal account.** Ask in a regular new chat with your usual memory and custom instructions. Repeat 5 times.
4. **Search forced on.** In any of the above, open the tools menu, select **View all tools** and then **Search**, as described in [OpenAI's web search help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), and ask again. Repeat 5 times and open the Sources panel.

For every run, write down the brands named, in order, and whether citations appeared. Then count how many of the 5 runs mention each brand in each condition.

In our experience, the wording changes every time, the top few brands are fairly stable, the brands further down the list come and go, and search-enabled answers can bring in names (and sources) that never appear otherwise. Your own account may lean toward topics you've discussed before. Exact results will depend on your category, so treat your own tally, not anyone's prediction, as the finding.

## What this means for brand visibility

If ChatGPT's answer isn't fixed, "where do we rank in ChatGPT?" is the wrong question. The useful questions are:

- **How often are we mentioned?** Your *mention rate*: the share of runs, across a set of prompts, in which your brand appears. For example, appearing in 7 of 10 runs is a strong position; 1 of 10 is fragile, even if that one run looked great in a screenshot.
- **How prominent are we when mentioned?** First recommendation or an afterthought?
- **How do we compare?** Your share of mentions versus competitors on the same prompts.
- **Is it stable?** A real change persists across several rounds of testing. A one-off swing is often just sampling noise.

In practice that means a fixed prompt set, clean sessions, several runs per prompt and comparison over time. For the bigger strategic picture, see our [AI brand visibility guide](/blog/ai-brand-visibility-guide).

Manual testing gets slow fast: 20 prompts, 5 runs each and 4 assistants is 400 answers per round. That is why tools exist to automate it. AI Brand Track queries ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini with prompts relevant to your industry and reports a 0-100 visibility score, which prompts mention you, competitor rankings, sentiment and share of voice. See how it works on the [AI rank tracker](/ai-rank-tracker) page. Like any tool, it measures a sample of answers rather than every possible answer, so treat results as trends to watch, not a fixed rank.

## FAQ

### Is everyone's ChatGPT different?

To a degree, yes. The underlying model is the same for users on the same version, but [memory](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt), custom instructions, chat history, location, plan and feature rollouts mean each person's ChatGPT can respond differently. Built-in randomness adds further variation even for the same user.

### If you ask ChatGPT the same question twice, will you get the same answer?

Usually not word for word. As [OpenAI explains](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed), ChatGPT samples each word from a range of likely options, so wording, order and sometimes substance change between runs. In our experience, well-established facts tend to stay consistent, while lists and recommendations vary more.

### Why does ChatGPT give different answers to the same question?

The main reasons are sampling randomness, different or updated models, memory and custom instructions, earlier messages in the conversation, whether a web search ran (and what it found) and your location or language. Any of these can change the answer on its own.

### Are ChatGPT answers unique?

Each response is generated fresh rather than retrieved from a stored list, so the exact wording is usually unique to that run. That doesn't make it original research: the content still comes from patterns in training data and, when search is used, from the pages it cites.

### Does ChatGPT usually agree with you?

It can lean toward the framing of your question. A prompt like "Why is Brand X the best?" invites a more positive answer than "What are the pros and cons of Brand X?" Phrase questions neutrally if you want a balanced view, and keep wording identical when you test brand visibility.

### Does ChatGPT give better answers if you are polite?

We haven't found OpenAI guidance saying politeness changes answer quality. What reliably helps is clarity: say what you need, give context (audience, budget, location) and ask for sources when accuracy matters.

### How can brands measure ChatGPT visibility if answers change?

Measure rates, not single answers. Run a fixed set of buyer-style prompts several times in clean sessions, record how often your brand appears, its position and which competitors show up, and compare the numbers over time. AI visibility tools such as AI Brand Track can automate the repeated runs across several assistants.
